text:
olivia: Heads-up — after unmuting the fused-paged-attn v2 kernel on SM90 (CUDA 13 canary) we see a big tail-latency spike on long-seq requests. Noticed in prod canary.
raj: numbers? what workload?
olivia: quick paste from the canary run: 
```
canary: fused-paged-attn v2 (cuda kernel)
hw: SM90, CUDA 13.1
workload: chat long-seq (prompt+gen ~4096 tokens)
baseline (paged-fused v1): p50 3.2ms, p95 8.1ms, p99 12.0ms
canary (v2):            p50 3.4ms, p95 18.7ms, p99 46.3ms
notes: increased variance after ~2k seq length
```
marta: I pulled a trace with nvprof — looks like L2 miss rate jumps and kernel elapsed time per call doubles for fused_paged_attention_v2. snippet: 
```
Kernel: fused_paged_attention_v2
SharedMemUtil: 72%
L2 hit rate: 0.62 -> 0.38
Elapsed per-call: 0.8ms -> 2.4ms (for long QKV chunks)
```
sophie: this smells like batching + page eviction thrash. our dynamic-batcher is still allowing very large batch_token sizes for long-seq traffic. can we clamp max_batch_tokens or change batching heuristic for canary?
raj: also, did Triton fallback kick in? I remember triton vs cuda kernel selection logic has a corner where triton gets chosen on some SM90+CUDA combos.
olivia: good call — logs show mixed kernels: a subset of hosts fell back to triton-interop path due to a kernel launch failure then retried the cuda kernel -> extra syncs. those retried requests line up with the p99 spikes.
marta: nvprof shows more global memory traffic on those hosts — possible register spill or different tiling on SM90 with cuda13. here's the eviction counter from runtime metrics: 
```
kv_page_evictions: baseline 120/min -> canary 880/min
kv_prefetch_hits: 4% -> 1%
batcher_max_tokens observed: 24576 (huge)
```
perf-bot: Created perf issue #4421 and uploaded canary trace bundle (link: https://perf.redwood/4421) :thinking_face:
raj: mitigation steps: 1) roll back fused-paged v2 on SM90 hosts, 2) clamp batcher max_batch_tokens to 8192 for long-seq traffic, 3) add KV-prefetch into request path to reduce cold-page misses, 4) schedule detailed CUPTI profile.
sophie: I can push a hotfix to the batching heuristic today — change is small: clamp tokens if seq_len > 2048 and scale down dynamic_batch_timeout. also add an opt-out flag for fused-paged where we force the triton kernel path for suspect builds.
olivia: can we roll the rollback quickly? I don't want more users hit while we dig.
deploy-bot: Canary rollback started for fused-paged-attn v2 on SM90 groups. Rolling to previous kernel (paged-fused v1).
raj: after rollback + batching clamp in test: 
```
post-fix bench (stress long-seq): p50 3.3ms, p95 9.1ms, p99 13.5ms
kv_page_evictions: down to 150/min
```
olivia: nice. we'll keep the canary off for SM90+CUDA13 for now and investigate register spilling/tiling mismatch. planning a deeper CUPTI run Monday to capture bank conflicts and shared mem patterns.
marta: created branch runtime/sm90-fused-fallback-fixes with a KV-prefetch patch + batch clamp, putting up PR now.
perf-bot: Linked PR #789 to perf issue #4421. :thumbsup:
olivia: thanks all. follow-up action items: (1) CUPTI profiling Monday, (2) microbench tile-size sweep on dev cluster, (3) verify triton vs cuda heuristics don't flip unexpectedly. I'll post results in this thread.
raj: ack
sophie: ack
deploy-bot: Canary fully rolled back at 2361234599
olivia: closing the hot canary incident for now, leaving the PRs and traces for the Monday deep dive.
